findings.title: Deleting the cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing the deleted cache
findings.body:
The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (`onChanged` from the wrapper). It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. That query is the source of `cacheUpdatedAt`, and it runs with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`.

Wherever `onChanged` is not passed, or does not refetch that query, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated: …" and the "Delete cached data" action after a successful deletion.

The disconnect mutation in the same component does invalidate this query in `onSettled`. `deleteCacheMutation` should invalidate it the same way.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data likely doesn't touch updatedAt and adds an unused write on every cache refresh
findings.body:
`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is meant to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. As far as I know, Prisma only applies `@updatedAt` when at least one field is being set; with `data: {}` the update is a no-op, so the timestamp probably never changes.

Even if it did work, nothing reads this value: the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, and the PR notes themselves question it.

The call also adds an extra DB round-trip to every webhook-driven `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` and to the unwatch path. If it throws, it fails the webhook after the cache was already written. Either pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly or remove the call.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires unused updatedAt/googleChannelId fields, widening the public input contract
findings.body:
`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. This function is also exported as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` for `@calcom/platform-libraries`. Any caller that builds the user with a narrower selectedCalendars select will stop type-checking.

No code in this PR reads these fields. To satisfy the type, `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `user.ts` (lines 899-900) now selects them on every session load. This puts `googleChannelId` (the webhook channel identifier) into `ctx.user` for no functional reason.

Drop these additions unless they are actually consumed.

findings.title: Authorization failure thrown as plain Error surfaces as 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
findings.body:
When the credential doesn't exist or belongs to another user, the handler throws a plain `new Error(...)`. tRPC maps this to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so an expected access-denied or not-found case gets logged and reported as a server fault.

Other handlers use `TRPCError` with `code: "NOT_FOUND"` or `"FORBIDDEN"` so clients and monitoring can tell these cases apart. The same should be done here.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired entries that are never served
findings.body:
`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all `CalendarCache` rows for the credential, with no `expiresAt` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`.

A credential whose cache rows have all expired therefore still shows "Last updated: …" and a delete option, which suggests a usable cache exists. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the where clause if the status is meant to reflect the active cache.

findings.title: Stale migration warning and misleading backfilled timestamps
findings.body:
The header comment says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty". The SQL actually adds `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the leftover warning is wrong and will confuse anyone reviewing migrations.

The default also stamps every pre-existing cache row with the migration time. After deploy, the new UI will report "Last updated" as the deploy time for legacy caches that may be weeks old, until each row is next upserted.

findings.title: Timestamp formatting hardcodes en-US locale
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)`. All users therefore see US date order and 12h time, regardless of their locale (`useLocale`) or their 12/24h `timeFormat` setting. The surrounding label is translated, but the date inside it is not. Use the user's locale, or the existing dayjs/time-format helpers.

findings.title: BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks the script on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU sed, `''` is taken as the (empty) script and the substitution expression is taken as a filename. The command fails with "can't read s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...", so on Linux an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` entry is never updated. The script still prints "✅ Updated" afterwards.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's cwd, and failure paths exit 0
findings.body:
`ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the current working directory, not the script's location. Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root (the usual way) touches or creates a `.env` in the parent directory of the repository instead of the repo's own `.env`. It should resolve relative to `$(dirname "$0")`.

Separately, `cleanup` always ends with `exit 0`. The rate-limit and "failed to extract URL" paths therefore report success to callers.

findings.title: dev:cron now relies on an undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
findings.body:
`dev:cron` was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` isn't in this package's dependencies. `npx` will download whatever version is current from the registry at run time. That is non-reproducible and fails offline.

The change is also unrelated to this feature, and the other scripts in this file still use the declared `ts-node`.
